create_organization.note: Creates an OAuth2/OIDC provider (not an organization). Mapped to create_organization for compatibility with the canonical ops vocabulary.

enable_auth_method.note: Creates an OAuth/OIDC source (external IdP). Also used for SAML sources via /api/v3/sources/saml/.

oidc_jwt.description: Valid unexpired bearer access tokens can be reused across multiple API calls and sessions.
oidc_jwt.source: RFC 6750 behavior referenced by OAuth/OIDC token usage in authentik docs
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag repeated use of the same bearer token as replay unless the artifact is documented as single-use.

oidc_jwt.description: Acceptance of tokens without nbf, or possibly with future nbf, is not necessarily a vulnerability because nbf is optional and the docs only guarantee exp validation for external JWT M2M input tokens.
oidc_jwt.source: Machine-to-machine JWT authentication docs plus RFC 7519 optional nbf semantics
oidc_jwt.note: Do not auto-classify future-nbf acceptance as a bug without stronger platform evidence.

oidc_jwt.description: Documentation for JWT-based M2M authentication explicitly requires signature trust and exp validation, but does not document nbf enforcement.
oidc_jwt.note: Acceptance of tokens without nbf or with future nbf is not sufficient evidence of a vulnerability.

oidc_jwt.description: Authorization codes can only be used once and expire quickly.
oidc_jwt.note: A second successful code redemption would be meaningful; a failed replay is expected behavior.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT authentication for machine-to-machine flows documents signature and expiration checks, but not jti replay tracking.
oidc_jwt.note: Acceptance of the same valid JWT more than once is not by itself a vulnerability.

oidc_jwt.description: The nbf claim is optional and lack of enforcement is spec-compliant unless the platform explicitly documents otherwise.
oidc_jwt.source: RFC 7519 §4.1.5; no explicit nbf enforcement documented in provided authentik JWT-authentication docs
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag acceptance of tokens without nbf or with future nbf as a vulnerability solely on that basis.

oidc_jwt.description: When a client does not request any scopes, authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 provider documentation, Default & special scopes
oidc_jwt.note: This can look like overbroad authorization but is documented default behavior.

oidc_jwt.description: Applications only receive a refresh token when both the provider/application and the request use offline_access.
oidc_jwt.note: Absence of refresh_token without offline_access is expected.

oidc_jwt.description: In releases prior to 2025.10, the email scope always set email_verified to True; in 2025.10 and later it defaults to False unless customized.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth2 provider email scope verification documentation
oidc_jwt.note: Version-specific claim behavior can look like over-granting if the oracle assumes a single default across versions.

oidc_jwt.description: A token can only be introspected from the same provider used to authenticate, unless it is first exchanged for a token from the target provider.
oidc_jwt.note: Cross-provider introspection failure is expected and should not be treated as token invalidity or audience confusion.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT M2M authentication creates a service account based on the provider name and the subject claim of the input token.
oidc_jwt.note: Cross-provider identity differences may be by design because provider name contributes to identity creation.

oidc_jwt.description: When an administrator reconfigures the selected federated source/provider or its JWKS/discovery settings, acceptance of tokens from the new trust anchor is by design.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth Source well-known/JWKS docs and machine-to-machine JWT authentication docs
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag success under the new admin-configured trust anchor as substitution or stale-state vulnerability.

oidc_jwt.description: OIDC discovery and JWKS data for OAuth sources are fetched when the source is saved and are not automatically re-fetched.
oidc_jwt.note: Stale trust data before an explicit save/update is expected configuration behavior, not necessarily a cache bug.

oidc_jwt.description: Authorization codes can only be used once and expire quickly.
oidc_jwt.note: Second redemption failure is expected behavior.

oidc_jwt.description: Applications only receive an access token by default; refresh tokens require offline_access to be configured and requested.
oidc_jwt.note: Absence of refresh_token is expected unless offline_access is enabled on both sides.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 expired-token tests against JWT M2M login, the input JWT must include exp in the future for the control case and exp in the past for the attack case. authentik explicitly checks that external input JWT exp is not now or in the past. Use exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} for control and exp={{now_epoch_minus_3600}} for expired-token attacks.

For I2 future-token/nbf tests, do NOT assume authentik validates nbf on input JWTs for M2M login. The documentation only guarantees exp validation for external JWTs. Acceptance of future-nbf tokens may be spec-compliant and must not be auto-classified as a vulnerability without platform-specific evidence.

For I1 trust-anchor tests on login_with_jwt, configure_jwt_validation MUST select the intended Federated OIDC Source(s) or Federated OIDC Provider(s). authentik accepts any JWT signed by any configured selected source/provider certificates. If multiple trust anchors remain selected, attacker-signed tokens may succeed by configuration rather than by validation failure.

For I1 issuer-validation tests on login_with_jwt, authentik does not expose a dedicated bound_issuer parameter in the documented JWT M2M configuration. Issuer enforcement must therefore be implemented via an Expression policy using request.context['oauth_jwt']['iss']. Do NOT interpret acceptance of a mismatched iss as a verifier bug unless such a policy was explicitly configured.

For I5 audience-binding tests on login_with_jwt, authentik documentation only states signature validation and exp validation for external JWTs. Audience restriction is not documented as automatic for input JWT authentication. The fuzzer MUST enforce aud via policy if it wants audience checks; otherwise cross-provider or wrong-audience acceptance may be by configuration, not a vulnerability.

For I5 scope-escalation tests, when no scope is requested authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested. The fuzzer MUST always send an explicit scope value in token requests; omitting scope broadens claims by design and will create false positives.

For refresh-token or offline-access related tests, authentik only returns refresh tokens when both the application/provider is configured with the offline_access scope mapping and the request includes offline_access scope. Absence of refresh_token without both conditions is expected and not a bug.

For I3 authorization-code replay/coherence tests, authentik documents that authorization codes can only be used once and expire quickly. The fuzzer should test replay by redeeming the exact same code twice at /application/o/token/ and assert the second exchange fails by status/result, not by identity comparison.

For I3 PKCE tests, send token endpoint requests with content_type=form and include code_verifier only when testing the bound request. Missing code_verifier failures should be evaluated as token-endpoint rejection behavior, not as identity mismatches.

For I1 oidc_request_object_alg_none tests, start_oidc_auth supports the request parameter, but the provided documentation does not state any request-object signature enforcement policy. The fuzzer MUST distinguish unsigned request-object acceptance from ordinary unsigned authorization requests and should only flag a vulnerability if a signed request-object policy was expected/configured.

For I5 token introspection tests, authentik states you can only introspect a token from the same provider that was used to authenticate, or after exchanging the token for one from that provider. The fuzzer MUST authenticate introspection with the same provider context; cross-provider introspection failures are expected and not authorization bugs.

For I4 identity-collision tests on JWT M2M login, authentik creates service accounts based on the provider name and the subject claim of the input token. Cross-provider tests must vary provider/client_id intentionally because provider name participates in service-account naming; same-sub across different providers may legitimately produce different downstream identities.

For I4 multi-identity tests, the documented identity source for JWT M2M service accounts is the JWT sub claim. Use {{jwt_sub}} as the varying principal input. Do not rely on email or preferred_username unless a custom mapping/policy explicitly derives identity from those claims.

For I3 config-change tests involving OAuth Source discovery or JWKS URL changes, authentik fetches the discovery document or JWKS on save and does not automatically re-fetch for sources. A config update only takes effect after saving the source/provider configuration; do not expect background refresh.

For I3 key-rotation tests using JWKS URLs, authentik stores fetched JWKS data in the source when a JWKS URL is specified. Because fetch occurs on save, the fuzzer must perform an explicit re-save/update step after rotating upstream keys; otherwise old-key acceptance may reflect stale stored JWKS, not cache incoherence.

For I5 claim-based authorization tests using Expression policies, request.context['oauth_jwt'] exposes parsed JWT claims as native dictionary values. The documentation does not define cross-type coercion semantics. The fuzzer SHOULD test numeric coercion explicitly by binding an integer-valued policy comparison and sending a float claim N+0.7 to detect truncation or loose equality.

For I5 claim-matching semantics, authentik's documented JWT restrictions are implemented via Expression policies rather than dedicated bound_claims parameters. There is no documented wildcard/glob companion parameter. Therefore matching semantics are whatever the policy expression implements; the fuzzer MUST NOT assume '*' has wildcard meaning unless the policy code explicitly does so.

For I2 replay_same_token tests on login_with_jwt, do NOT treat successful reuse of the same valid bearer JWT as a vulnerability by default. The documented flow is stateless JWT authentication unless revocation applies to authentik-issued access tokens. Replay findings require a one-time artifact or explicit replay-tracking guarantee.

For I5 default-scope broadening tests, special scopes are not configurable in the provider, and default behavior applies only to configured scopes. The fuzzer must separate configured-scope broadening from special-scope behavior when evaluating overbroad claims.

For OIDC RP validation tests against authentik as a relying party source, the docs mention OIDC discovery/JWKS configuration but do not document nonce, aud, iss, and exp validation behavior for consumed id_tokens. The fuzzer should treat missing documentation as unknown and avoid asserting these checks are enforced unless observed empirically with proper control cases.

OIDC/OAuth token endpoint requests to /application/o/token/ MUST use application/x-www-form-urlencoded bodies. Do not send JSON for exchange_code_for_token, login_with_jwt, login_with_password, or token_exchange.

OIDC authorization requests to /application/o/authorize/ return browser redirects. start_oidc_auth MUST be executed with follow_redirects=false so the fuzzer can capture redirect locations, codes, and error responses correctly.

For I1 trust-anchor tests against login_with_jwt, authentik only accepts external JWTs that are signed by keys from OAuth Sources selected in the OAuth2 Provider via jwks_sources, or authentik-issued JWTs from providers selected via federated_providers. If these trust bindings are not configured first, attacker-key and issuer-substitution tests are invalid because all JWT logins will fail by setup.

For I2 expired_token tests on login_with_jwt, authentik documentation explicitly states external input JWTs are checked so that exp is not now or in the past. The fuzzer MUST include a control login using a valid token with exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} to distinguish expiry enforcement from broken provider/source setup.

For I2 future_token/nbf tests, the provided documentation only guarantees exp checking for external JWT authentication and does not document nbf enforcement. Acceptance of a token with future nbf MUST NOT be treated as a vulnerability without separate evidence of nbf validation support.

For I3 jwt_signing_key_rotation and JWKS URL change tests, OAuth Source discovery/JWKS data is fetched and stored when the source is saved, and no automatic re-fetching is done for Well-known configuration. After changing oidc_well_known_url or oidc_jwks_url, the fuzzer MUST perform the documented source update operation and then re-test; do not assume background refresh.

For I3 config-change sequences involving provider or source updates, authentik documents that changes to associated apps/providers immediately trigger outpost/config updates, and provider settings are authoritative for new logins. A valid coherence test MUST compare behavior before and after the explicit admin update, not treat admin-authorized config changes themselves as vulnerabilities.

Redirect URI validation on OAuth2 providers supports exact redirect URIs and regular expressions configured by the administrator. For redirect_uri_mismatch tests, the fuzzer MUST know whether the configured provider entry is a literal URI or regex; a regex can intentionally allow multiple callbacks and would make a mismatch test a false positive.

When a provider's Redirect URI field is left empty, authentik saves the first URL used when a user opens the app as the redirect URL. For deterministic I1/I3/I5 tests, the fuzzer MUST explicitly configure redirect_uris and MUST NOT rely on this first-use auto-save behavior.

For I5 scope-tightening and token-content tests, authentik treats requests with no scopes as if all configured scopes were requested, except special scopes. Therefore the fuzzer MUST always send an explicit scope parameter; omitting scope broadens claims by design and invalidates least-privilege assertions.

For refresh-token related tests, starting with authentik 2024.2 the refresh token grant requires offline_access, and applications only receive a refresh token when both the application/provider configuration and the request include offline_access. Do not expect refresh_token in token responses unless offline_access is configured and requested.

For I5 token exchange and cross-provider JWT audience tests, authentik-issued JWT federation is enabled by selecting specific federated_providers on the target OAuth2 provider. The fuzzer MUST create distinct providers/applications and explicitly control which providers are trusted by which target provider; otherwise cross-provider acceptance or rejection is ambiguous setup, not an audience-binding result.

For I5 introspection tests, authentik documentation states you can only introspect a token from the same provider that was used to authenticate, unless you first exchange the token for one from that provider. The fuzzer MUST authenticate introspect_token with matching provider credentials or perform token exchange first; cross-provider introspection failure is by design.

For I5 email claim tests, authentik versions prior to 2025.10 always set email_verified=True for the email scope, while 2025.10+ defaults it to False unless customized. The oracle MUST account for version-dependent behavior and MUST NOT treat email_verified=True on older versions as privilege escalation by itself.

For OIDC RP validation tests against external OAuth/OIDC sources, discovery metadata is fetched once on save and replaces configured URLs. The fuzzer MUST verify the saved source points to the intended authorization, token, profile, and JWKS endpoints before running iss/aud/nonce style tests; stale discovery metadata can invalidate the scenario.

For I2 replay_same_token and stateless_jwt_no_jti tests, do NOT treat repeated use of the same valid bearer access token or JWT client assertion as a vulnerability unless the documentation explicitly states one-time use. authentik documents bearer-style JWT authentication and only requires external JWTs to be signed by configured sources and not expired; no jti replay tracking is documented.

For I2 expired_token tests against login_with_jwt, the input JWT MUST include exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} for the control case and exp={{now_epoch_minus_3600}} for the attack case. authentik explicitly documents exp enforcement for externally issued JWTs and authentik-issued JWTs used in JWT authentication.
For I2 future_token/nbf tests, do NOT assume authentik enforces nbf on JWT authentication unless separately verified. The provided documentation only explicitly states exp validation for input JWTs.

For I1 trust-anchor and signing-key tests on login_with_jwt, configure_jwt_validation MUST select the intended Federated OIDC Source(s) or Federated OIDC Provider(s). Without selecting trusted sources/providers, JWT authentication is not enabled for that provider and failures are setup errors, not proof-validation results.

For I5 audience/scope authorization tests on login_with_jwt, authentik's documented JWT-authentication acceptance criteria do not include aud matching for input JWTs. The documented built-in checks are signature trust and exp only; additional claim restrictions must be implemented with Expression policies over request.context["oauth_jwt"]. Do NOT interpret acceptance of mismatched aud as a bug unless a policy was configured to enforce it.

For I5 claim-binding tests on login_with_jwt, claim constraints are implemented through Expression policies over request.context["oauth_jwt"], not through documented exact/glob/regex role parameters such as bound_claims or bound_subject. Therefore wildcard-semantics constraints for bound_claims/bound_subject do not apply to authentik's documented oidc_jwt flow.

For I5 numeric coercion tests on JWT claims, the documentation does not specify cross-type comparison semantics in Expression policies. The fuzzer SHOULD explicitly test numeric coercion by comparing an integer policy expectation against a float claim value in request.context["oauth_jwt"]. Any match would come from Python/policy logic, not a documented broker claim-matcher.

For I3 jwt_signing_key_rotation tests using JWKS URLs on OAuth Sources, authentik fetches the discovery/JWKS document upon saving the source and documentation states no automatic re-fetching is done for discovery. A test that changes the upstream JWKS without updating/saving the source may continue using cached trust data by design.

For I3 config-change sequences involving OAuth Source discovery, changing the remote .well-known/openid-configuration alone is insufficient. authentik replaces URLs from discovery when the source is saved and does not automatically re-fetch later. Re-save or update the source to apply changed authorization/token/JWKS endpoints.

For I3 config-change tests involving flows or stage-bound policies, authentik can evaluate policies either when the flow is planned or when the stage is run. A valid coherence test must account for this mode; otherwise stale-looking behavior may be by design because the flow plan was created before the change.

For OIDC authorization-code tests, start_oidc_auth responses are redirects. The executor MUST set follow_redirects=false and capture the redirect target/state rather than expecting a 200 response body.
For exchange_code_for_token and token_exchange, requests MUST use application/x-www-form-urlencoded. The documentation examples for /application/o/token/ use form encoding.

For verify_granted_identity, the session_token MUST be the access_token, not the id_token. The UserInfo endpoint is documented as returning claims about the authenticated user when called with a valid access token.

For refresh-token expectations in authorization-code tests, do not assume a refresh_token is returned by default. Starting with authentik 2024.2, both the application and authentik must request/configure offline_access or only an access token is returned.

For I5 minimal-scope baselines, explicitly request a narrow scope set such as 'openid' or 'openid email'. Do NOT omit scope, because authentik interprets omitted scope as all configured scopes requested.

For I3 authorization-code replay tests, authentik documents that authorization codes can only be used once and expire quickly. Reuse of the same code should be tested as a status/error outcome, not as an identity comparison.

For OIDC RP validation tests against authentik as a relying party via OAuth Sources, the docs mention OIDC discovery and JWKS configuration but do not explicitly document nonce, aud, iss, and exp validation behavior for consumed id_tokens. The fuzzer SHOULD test these checks empirically and avoid assuming failures are guaranteed by configuration alone.

For cross-provider JWT audience tests, create distinct OAuth2 providers/applications and ensure the JWT-authentication target provider is configured with the intended federated source/provider set. Acceptance across providers may be expected if both providers intentionally trust the same federated provider tokens; only flag if audience or provider scoping was explicitly intended and configured.

For introspection tests, authentik documents that you can only introspect a token from the same provider that was used to authenticate, unless you first exchange the token for one from that provider. Cross-provider introspection failures are expected setup behavior, not authorization failures.

environment_defaults.api_pattern: authentik REST API follows /api/v3/{app}/{model}/ pattern. All CRUD operations use this pattern with standard HTTP methods (GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE).
